item.title: Shane Parish Recontextualizes Techno on Ingenious LP
item.description: Shane Parish thrives on conceiving projects that seem contradictory and overly challenging, yet come off as effortless and innovative.

item.title: Mitski Disappears with Grace on Eighth Album
item.description: On her eighth album, Nothing's About to Happen to Me, singer-songwriter Mitski employs a country-folk sound to reflect the peace found in isolation.

item.title: Xiu Xiu’s Jamie Stewart Is All Covered Up on New Record
item.description: Born from a cover-song subscription model, Xiu Xiu's latest album unearths the raw humanity in pop confections. Jamie Stewart discusses this and more.

item.title: Alice Coltrane: Conjurer of the Majestic
item.description: Andy Beta's Alice Coltrane biography, Cosmic Music, is an excellent work about this forward-thinking and often misunderstood musician.

item.title: Gorillaz at 25 Are a Cultural Force for the Good
item.description: Assuming personal stability is necessary for collective betterment, it's high time that Gorillaz share their newest, loving, bizarre journey with the rest of the world.

item.title: Armbruster Gleefully Confounds Expectations, Again
item.description: Connor Armbruster is not only a brilliant musician but a refreshingly restless one Half My House is a unique and tuneful spin on traditional Irish music

item.title: Fågelle Finds Melancholy Release in Glorious Gloom
item.description: Glorious gloom permeates the musical catalogue of Swedish singer-songwriter Fågelle, and her album Bränn min jord overflows with it.

item.title: The Complacent Bliss of Bruno Mars
item.description: Bruno Mars' fourth solo album, The Romantic, is as impeccably crafted as ever, but says nothing new about his place in the world of pop.

item.title: The Messthetics and James Brandon Lewis Create Ecstatic Post-Hardcore Jazz
item.description: The Messthetics and James Brandon Lewis make fearless and non-smooth fusion with the clarity and dynamism of "post-hardcore" that wasn't around in the 1970s.

item.title: Jay-Z’s 1999 Album ‘Vol. 3’ Is His Most Aggressive
item.description: In Jay-Z's Vol. 3… Life & Times of S. Carter, the ever-undeterred MC sounds anything but as he fulminates on one end and tightens his durag on the other.
